title: 27% of US Workers Using Savings to Cover Expenses
paragraphs: Many American workers are finding it difficult to pay for their daily needs with their salaries alone, and some are using their savings to fill the gap.

According to a survey by Talker Research published in October, more than a quarter of American workers, or 27%, said they had unexpectedly had to move money out of their savings account. The problem seems to be even more serious for people who are paid by the hour. Over a third of hourly workers, 34%, said they had used their savings to pay for everyday necessities such as groceries, medicine and gas.

Savings accounts are usually meant for emergencies or for long-term goals, such as buying a home or retiring. When people use them to pay for regular expenses, it can be a sign that their income is not keeping up with the cost of living.

Other recent research also shows that many workers have very little money to fall back on. A 2026 report by the insurance and consulting company Gallagher found that 27% of employees have no emergency savings at all. Another 24% have saved less than three months of expenses. Financial experts often recommend keeping enough savings to cover at least three months of living costs.
Without savings, an unexpected cost, such as a car repair or a medical bill, can cause serious problems. People in this situation may need to borrow money or use credit cards, which can lead to debt.

Some employers are trying to help. For example, some companies now offer financial education or programs that make it easier for workers to save part of their pay. However, these benefits are still not common.
The findings suggest that rising prices continue to put pressure on many American households, even when people have full-time jobs.
